sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (PRC) - as the formation seat of the WFOE; Taiwan (TW) is the investor's home jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with Chinese socialist legal characteristics)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) between the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits and the Straits Exchange Foundation (2010)
Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion (2012)
Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (as revised and effective 1 January 2025); Beneficial Owner Information Administrative Measures (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the PRC (2018 Amendment); Foreign Investment Law (2019) and its Implementing Regulations; Regulations on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration (2021 revision)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Commercial Department
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait exclusive authentication channel: Taiwan notary public notarization, then Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification, then Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) confirmation and filing with the PRC business registration authorities. This is the operative parallel to consular legalization; the Hague Apostille Convention does not apply to documents originating from Taiwan. No chain of both systems is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Commercial Department, or the local competent business registry in Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait exclusive authentication channel: SEF/ARATS verification following Taiwan notarization as described above; not subject to Hague Apostille. This consular-equivalent path is the sole mandatory legalization route for Taiwan-issued corporate certificates.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter evidencing financial standing of the Taiwan investing company and its main banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed commercial bank in Taiwan authorized by the Financial Supervisory Commission R.O.C. (Taiwan)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued on bank letterhead, notarized by a Taiwan notary public, then verified by SEF and confirmed by ARATS (cross-strait consular-equivalent legalization). The Hague Apostille path is inapplicable to bank instruments originating from Taiwan.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the legal representative of the WFOE in Mainland China and authorizing the deposition of incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Resolution signed by directors, certified before a Taiwan notary public, then submitted to SEF for verification and ARATS for confirmation. This cross-strait verification sequence is the exclusive mandatory authentication path; it does not use the Hague Apostille mechanism.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the Articles of Association (Charter) of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investing company or its Taiwan-licensed counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticated copy notarized by a Taiwan notary, followed by SEF verification and ARATS confirmation. Documents derived from Taiwan are not eligible for the Hague Apostille Convention and are instead processed through the bilateral cross-strait notarization mechanism; the two paths must not be combined or sequentially applied.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shadow directors, beneficial owners, persons with significant control, and authorized signatories of the Taiwan investing entity and the proposed Mainland WFOE must undergo enhanced due diligence prior to incorporation. The screening protocol mandates verification against: (i) the People's Bank of China (PBOC) domestic money laundering and terror-financing watchlists; (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list ( encompassing all frozen asset designations); (iii) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and sectoral sanctions lists; (iv) the European Union and United Kingdom consolidated financial sanctions lists; (v) domestic administrative credit and black-list databases of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); and (vi) a global politically exposed persons (PEP) database (e.g., World-Check or equivalent). Automated screening must run continuously, with a refresh interval not exceeding 24 hours during the formation phase and throughout the operational life of the WFOE. Any positive hit, unresolved discrepancy, or unusual negative news triggers mandatory escalation to the designated AML Compliance Officer, who shall document the likelihood determination and record a reasoned approval or rejection in the client risk file. In all cases, the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner is disclosed to the appropriate government registry only, in line with the PBOC Order No. 3 beneficial-owner confidentiality regime.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and the independent Enterprise Name Pre-approval System administered by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via https://www.gsxt.gov.cn/ and the local SAMR online service portals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese statutory name must adopt the mandatory four-tier structure: (1) administrative division qualifier (optional for wholly foreign-owned enterprises); (2) unique transliterated or coined trademark/font characters; (3) industry or business scope description; and (4) the mandatory legal form suffix '有限公司' (limited liability company). All characters must be in simplified Chinese (GB 13000 / GB2312), and any romanized or pinyin form used in the English translation must exactly mirror the shareholder's identity documents without altering meaning. Trademark-style names may be registered if they do not mislead as to the enterprise's nature, and no foreign-language name may replace the statutory Chinese name. The English name, if used, is secondary and must be identical in meaning and transliteration across all regulatory filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed enterprise name, the applicant may file an administrative review request with the same registration authority within fifteen (15) business days of the rejection notice. The written request must state the legal basis, the grounds of non-conflict, and any supporting evidence, including trademark registration certificates or consents from prior rights holders. If the review is denied, the applicant may initiate an administrative reconsideration with the superior SAMR bureau within sixty (60) days of the denial, or alternatively file an administrative lawsuit before the competent People's Court within six (6) months of the same date. The entire appellate process can be completed online using the same portal, and the applicant may also submit a softened name variant simultaneously to avoid further delays. A formal rejection opinion must be issued by the SAMR official, and the reasons for refusal must be narrowly construed; failure to provide a written reason constitutes procedural violation warranting automatic reprocessing of the original name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding mailbox is strictly rejected for the registered office of a WFOE engaged in mail-order retail under ISIC 4791 with cash-on-delivery settlement. The PRC Company Law (Article 10) requires a real and continuous domicile, and SAMR registration will not approve an address that is not an exclusive leased or owned commercial premise. The local tax authority (State Taxation Administration) requires a physical site capable of storing accounting records, issuing electronic invoices, and receiving correspondence; a virtual address will trigger a tax registration suspension. Furthermore, commercial banks performing KYC for the cash-on-delivery collection network (including the target payment rails Airwallex and local logistics remittance) will refuse to open a corporate settlement account if the address is solely a virtual office, because the COD business model involves elevated cash-handling risk. Regional pilot programs that allow 'address hosting' (e.g., Shanghai Free Trade Zone) are limited to technology or services companies and do not extend to physical-goods COD retail. Therefore, a leased physical office with a red-seal lease certificate (红本租赁凭证) is mandatory for incorporation and for all subsequent bank and tax filings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: The probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by municipal tax or SAMR authorities during the first 18 months is quantified at 40-60% for cash-on-delivery e-commerce registrations. The inspection checklist includes: (i) presence of a physical address signboard matching the registered address; (ii) occupied workstations and accessible staff; (iii) original business license displayed; (iv) accounting ledgers, invoices, bank statements, and inventory records; (v) fire safety inspection certificate; (vi) original red-seal lease contract; (vii) VAT general taxpayer certificate and electronic tax-control equipment; and (viii) evidence of actual logistics activities. For virtual-office registrations, the risk score is 5 out of 5, resulting in an immediate entry into the 'business operating anomaly list' and revocation of invoice quotas. For fully operational physical offices, the risk score is 2 out of 5; non-rectification of any inspection finding leads to inclusion in the national credit blacklist and denial of senior management visa/re-entry permits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official business license and enterprise registration fee (no longer charged by SAMR for standard LLC registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), local market supervision bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government statutory fee abolished under the 2021 Administrative Reform; zero official registry charge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seal engraving set (company seal, financial seal, contract seal, invoice seal, legal representative seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed seal engraving enterprise approved by the provincial public security authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark tariff as regulated by local public security; typical 250-350 CNY (approx. USD 35-50) for full set.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-strait notarization and SEF/ARATS verification fees for the Taiwan investor corporate documentation (5 instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan notary, Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) and its designated PRC authentication office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary and verification tariffs under the Cross-Strait Agreement on Notarization; prevailing market rate for five instruments; variable between 300-450 USD.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel fees for drafting WFOE articles of association, preparing board resolutions, shareholder resolutions, and reviewing the entire incorporation dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC-licensed law firm engaged by the investor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for cross-border WFOE incorporation services; 1,000-2,500 USD depending on complexity and language requirement.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Chinese-translated documents by a PRC notary public (for business license copies, investor identity documents, and lease contract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC notary office located in the registration district
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Provincial price bureau notary fee schedule; typical 100-150 USD for a bundle of up to 10 pages.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical lease - first-year deposit and initial rent (minimum area 20 sqm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord or licensed property manager
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rent benchmark for Class B commercial premises in a non-tier-one city; approximate 500-700 USD per month; 6,000 USD covers first-year deposit and advance rent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration, social security registration, and accounting software setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) local office; social security bureau; third-party accounting software vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official government fee for tax and social security registration; software setup and initial data migration market rate 200-400 USD.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank corporate account opening package and KYC/AML compliance review (institution fee and document notarization)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank (target account opening bank) accepting the WFOE application
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff for corporate account onboarding; includes KYC verification (approx. 100-250 USD) depending on transaction volume projection and risk classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act, Articles 98 (limited liability company), 128 (shareholders), 154 (limited liability), 172 (board meetings), and 387 (company registration); Foreign Investment Act, Articles 5 and 6; Company Registration Regulations; Central Bank Foreign Exchange Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Company and Commercial Registration, Taiwan; with prior review by the Investment Review Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation filed through the MOEA Company and Commerce Registration Front-End System, accompanied by the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Taiwan WFOE limited liability company under ISIC 4791. The foreign investor must demonstrate adequate capitalization in the business plan reviewed by the Investment Review Commission. Paid-in capital must be remitted from abroad and evidenced by a bank certificate of inward remittance and a deposit balance certificate. No blocked escrow account is statutorily required for this e-commerce business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001 — FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] LIMITED, TAIWAN. THIS FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION is adopted unanimously in writing by the sole director and the subscriber(s) of [COMPANY] LIMITED, a limited liability company organized under the laws of Taiwan. WHEREAS the company has received Foreign Investment Approval and desires to complete its statutory incorporation, governance, and banking arrangements. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The authorized share capital of the company is [amount] New Taiwan Dollars, divided into [number] ordinary shares of [par value] each. The sole Shareholder, [Investor], hereby ratifies its subscription to all issued shares and confirms that the aggregate subscription price has been irrevocably paid in full by overseas remittance into the company's bank account. The Director is directed to register the paid-in capital with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, record all allotments in the share register, and furnish capital payment certificates. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The company shall open and maintain corporate bank and merchant accounts with [Bank]. The Director and the General Manager are hereby authorized, either jointly or singly, to execute account opening forms, mandates, credit facilities, standing instructions, wire transfer orders, and settlement agreements, and to engage banking agents reasonably necessary for the cash-on-delivery payment flow, including but not limited to Airwallex and local logistics remittance providers. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the company for statutory and tax purposes shall be located at [Taiwan registered address]. The Director is directed to execute the registered-office consent by the landlord, affix the corporate seal, complete business registration, and file any subsequent address change by board resolution. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The following appointments are made and accepted: [Name] as Director and Chairperson of the Board; [Name] as General Manager with day-to-day management powers; and [Name] as Company Secretary responsible for corporate records and statutory filings. The officers are expressly empowered to execute all documents, instruct lawyers and tax agents, negotiate agreements, and represent the company before authorities. 5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE. The fiscal year shall end on December 31. The annual financial statements shall be audited in accordance with Standards on Auditing in Taiwan. The corporate seal shall not be used unless accompanied by the Company Secretary's records entry. 6. GENERAL PROVISIONS. This resolution shall be conclusive evidence of the authorities granted and may be certified by the Director for use before banks, courts, government agencies, logistics partners, and tax authorities. This resolution is effective immediately upon signature and remains in force until rescinded or amended by a written board resolution. This resolution has been read and approved and is signed on the date first above written.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval by Investment Review Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Review Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (online Foreign Investment Approval portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a signed Foreign Investment Application through the MOEA Investment Review Commission online portal, identifying the applicant, business scope under ISIC 4791, proposed capital, and local corporate name. If the shareholder is a foreign company, enclose its certificate of incorporation, authorization, and board resolution. If the shareholder is an individual, enclose passport or overseas residence certificate. All documents must be in Chinese translation certified by a Taiwan notary or authorized translation institution. The Commission may request comments from the competent industry authority, but no industrial license is required for mail-order retail. Keep the approval certificate because it must be filed with the registry.
required_dossiers: Completed Foreign Investment Application Form
Investor's certificate of incorporation or passport
Board resolution of the foreign investor authorizing the Taiwan WFOE subscription
Power of attorney to a local agent or lawyer
Bank reference letter for the investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, file the requested supplementary evidence within the MOEA-prescribed response period, generally 30 days. If approval is suspended because of beneficiary-ownership or investor-screening questions, engage a Taiwan legal counsel to submit a written reply and attend a consultation. An administrative appeal may be filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs Appeals Committee within 30 days after written refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Clearance and Notarized Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Company and Commercial Registration, Taiwan (Company and Commerce Registration Front-End System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, conduct a name and business scope pre-check through the MOEA registration system. Execute the Articles of Incorporation before a Taiwan notary and include the FIA reference number, legal address, capital amount, director powers, and the permitted ISIC 4791 scope. Then file the company establishment registration electronically using the investor's bank certificate of inward remittance and a deposit balance certificate. The MOEA will issue the uniform tax number and Certificate of Company Registration. For WFOEs, any director's signature taken abroad must be notarized and authenticated, and the power of attorney must be lodged with the filing.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Certificate
Name and business scope pre-approval letter
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and shareholder written consent
Director identification documents
Certificate of inward remittance and bank deposit balance certificate
Registered office lease or landlord consent with building use permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a clarification, correct the defective attachments and re-submit through the front-end system within the notice period normally stated in the deficiency letter. If the application is refused because the business scope is overbroad, narrow the description to mail-order retail and cash-on-delivery settlement, obtain a revised FIA certificate, and re-file. The company may also file an administrative appeal to MOEA within 30 days from refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Labor, and National Health Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau in the jurisdiction of the registered office; local Bureau of Labor; National Health Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After company registration, apply for tax and invoice registration at the regional National Taxation Bureau in the jurisdiction of the registered office. Complete the tax identification and invoice purchase application so the company can issue uniform invoices for COD e-commerce sales. Register with the local labor insurance and national health insurance administration as an employer before hiring staff; the statutory business registration form must identify the responsible person and tax representative. Maintain payroll, VAT books, and inbound remittance files for future inspection by the National Taxation Bureau. An electronic tax registration is integrated with the company registration in most municipalities.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Company Registration and uniform tax number
Articles of Incorporation and shareholder directory
Responsible person and tax representative ID
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Proposed payroll and employment handbook if employees will be hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau rejects the invoice application because the responsible person has prior tax arrears or litigation, replace the responsible person by board resolution and re-apply. If labor registration is queried, submit the employment contract and compensation amendment within 14 days. A tax administrative reconsideration may be made within 30 days of any adverse determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening and Cash-on-Delivery Merchant Facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Taiwan bank's corporate banking and AML compliance unit; Financial Supervisory Commission as supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a Taiwan bank that offers corporate accounts for foreign-invested e-commerce and COD settlement. Submit the company's KYC and AML package, Board resolution on account signatories, beneficial ownership declaration, and explanations of the COD cash flow. The bank must perform enhanced due diligence because cash-on-delivery logistics can involve money-laundering risk; provide the logistics partner agreement, refund policy, expected monthly transaction volume, and details of Airwallex or local logistics remittance rails if used. Sign official account mandates and arrange for at least two authorized representatives. Obtain a letter of deposit or account statement to evidence paid-in capital and retain it for the registry.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Company Registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Foreign Investment Approval Certificate
Board resolution authorizing bank account signatories
Beneficial ownership declaration and corporate ownership chart
E-commerce platform and logistics provider agreements
AML/CFT internal control statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses due to risk concerns, request a written refusal, cure the attributed deficiencies by adding compliance policies or restricting COD settlement limits, and resubmit. If a second bank also declines, apply to a bank with cross-border payment expertise or file a complaint with the Financial Ombudsman Institution. A board resolution may designate an alternate authorized representative to avoid signature-impairment issues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Commercial Registration, Zoning Compliance, and Final Post-Incorporation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal government commercial registration window; local Public Works Department; local Fire Bureau; Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete municipal commercial registration in the city where the registered office is located if required by the local government. Obtain the building occupancy-use permit and submit proof of the lease. Because ISIC 4791 is mail-order retail, no industrial operating license or statutory EIA is required; however, if goods storage or consolidation is later introduced, apply to the local Fire Bureau for a low-hazard occupancy fire safety certificate and to the Public Works Department for use zoning approval before opening the space. Finally, establish the statutory AML/CFT internal control document and maintain a current register of ultimate beneficial owners at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Municipal commercial registration application form
Certificate of Company Registration
Lease contract and landlord's written consent
Building occupancy permit or use zoning certificate
AML/CFT internal control manual
Register of directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality questions land use, obtain a lawful-use certificate or an existing-use permit from the landlord, or apply for a temporary zoning permit. If the Fire Bureau requires remedial fire-equipment installation, engage a licensed fire-protection contractor and resubmit the certificate of inspection. If MOEA or municipal authorities require revised shareholder disclosures, file an amended beneficiary register with retrograde effect.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — ISIC 4791 is mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement and does not fall within ISIC groups 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx, or 52xx covering manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no industrial operating license is required for pure mail-order retail; only company registration, tax registration, municipal business registration, and banking approvals are required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable for the current scope. If the company later installs warehousing over environmental thresholds or engages in manufacturing, it must apply to the Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration and the local Bureau of Environmental Protection for an environmental registration or full EIA review, and comply with wastewater, VOC, and hazardous-waste discharge standards then applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for pure mail-order retail and cash-on-delivery e-commerce without a warehouse or assembly operation. If the company later handles physical goods, it must obtain a fire safety certificate from the local Fire Bureau (Civil Defense Division), a structural use approval from the municipal Public Works Department, and a workplace safety clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act before commencement.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); electronic registration and filing are conducted through the Electronic Tax Authority (E-Tax Bureau) portal at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn, together with the provincial electronic tax landing pages and the STA VAT Invoice Management System.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the resident CN WFOE: (1) complete incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation and obtain the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which serves as the statutory taxpayer identification number; (2) complete tax registration, taxpayer qualification, and tax-scope confirmation through the E-Tax Bureau within 30 calendar days of business license issuance; (3) complete VAT taxpayer type identification (small-scale or general), invoice type calibration, and the export tax refund/export tax exemption filing record before beginning export operations. For a foreign non-resident enterprise without a Chinese establishment that earns Chinese-source income or supplies taxable goods or services into China, the competent tax authority issues a Non-Resident Enterprise Taxpayer Identification Number through the E-Tax Bureau after the applicant provides the foreign corporate registration certificate, board resolutions, a tax residency certificate from the jurisdiction of residence, a China-nominated agent or withholding agent appointment letter, and documentary evidence of the Chinese-source taxable event.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification. China does not operate a check-the-box or comparable pass-through entity election regime for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise; a WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise taxed at entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. The separate VAT registration election between small-scale taxpayer and general taxpayer status is an indirect-tax registration choice, not an entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Provisional Regulations on Value-Added Tax and the STA export tax refund/exemption administration framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in annual VAT taxable sales for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; tax registration itself is required within 30 calendar days of business license issuance regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registered VAT taxpayers must issue invoices through the VAT Invoice Management System / STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform using an approved tax control device or a fully digitalized electronic invoice integration. Fully digitalized electronic invoices are uploaded in near-real time to the national electronic invoice platform with a unique invoice verification number, supporting anti-fraud duplicate-issuance checks. Enterprises with general VAT taxpayer status must use the special VAT invoice system; approved third-party e-invoicing service providers connect through STA-compliant APIs, and the Golden Tax System performs invoice clearance verification, false-invoice monitoring, and retrospective audit controls.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from the Chinese customs territory by a VAT general taxpayer that holds a valid export-tax-refund filing record are eligible for the 0% export VAT rate with refund or credit of input VAT. Qualifying cross-border e-commerce retail exports may use the 9610, 9710, 9810, or 1210 customs supervision regimes and, where applicable, the no-invoice exemption treatment. The exporter must demonstrate actual cross-border dispatch through customs, retain the export sale documentation, and provide evidence that the foreign-currency export proceeds were repatriated to China within the statutory period, including where cash-on-delivery proceeds are collected by local logistics remittance partners and paid through licensed cross-border payment rails such as Airwallex or an equivalent regulated institution.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration Form (customs export declaration / customs Bill of Entry equivalent) issued by China Customs with the customs declaration number
Bill of Lading or airway waybill or comparable carrier-issued cross-border transport document
Export commercial invoice and packing list
Export contract or confirmed mail-order/e-commerce order record

Export foreign exchange repatriation and collection verification record on the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) Goods Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System, supported by bank inward remittance and foreign exchange settlement records
VAT ordinary invoice for the export sale where applicable, and, for trading entities, the input special VAT invoice from the upstream Chinese supplier
Cash-on-delivery payment rail foreign exchange reconciliation statement from the licensed cross-border payment provider or local logistics remittance partner
Certificate of origin or domestic purchase documentation required by customs or the destination jurisdiction, including preferential trade certificates where applicable for exports to Taiwan
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities may scrutinize export declarations, transport documents, VAT invoices, and foreign exchange repatriation records through the Golden Tax System risk-monitoring modules and paperless export-tax-refund review. If export zero-rating or refund is found to be fraudulent, unsupported, or based on false documentation, the STA will disallow the zero-rating, claw back the refunded tax, assess late-payment surcharges, impose a penalty of one to five times the defrauded amount under the Law on Administration of Tax Levy and Collection, suspend the taxpayer's export tax refund processing for a statutory period, downgrade customs credit status, and may refer the matter for criminal investigation under PRC criminal and customs law for fraudulent export tax refund.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime for the New Taiwan dollar with the central bank actively smoothing disruptive or one-sided market flows. Current-account convertibility is broadly unrestricted for goods, services and ordinary trade-related remittances, while capital-account transactions require prior regulatory approval or post-remittance statistical filing through a licensed designated foreign-exchange bank. Inward direct capital contributions into a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise must be approved by the Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission and then settled through a local designated foreign-exchange bank under a central-bank foreign-exchange transaction report. Export receipts are freely retainable in approved foreign-currency deposit accounts, but every export transaction must be supported by trade documents and reported for central-bank statistics. Profit remittance to the ultimate parent in mainland China is lawful only after the WFOE files its audited Taiwan statutory financial statements, settles all corporate income and withholding tax liabilities, obtains the annual central-bank remittance validation and submits the foreign-investor capital registration certificate. In practice the dominant hurdles are tax clearance, a clean capital verification record, and proof that each dividend remittance matches distributable reserves; any residual capital-account reduction requires separate Investment Commission approval. Offshore digital or anonymous e-money channels are not recognised for statutory capital, tax clearance or customs purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must collect and settle export foreign-currency proceeds within 180 days from the date of shipment or loading; the proceeds may be retained in an approved foreign-currency deposit account at a designated foreign-exchange bank or converted into New Taiwan dollars at the prevailing market rate. There is no legislated minimum mandatory conversion ratio; the exporter has full discretion to retain 100% of the foreign currency, provided the inward remittance is correctly classified, supported by export documentation and reported to the central bank through the depositary bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore electronic money institutions such as Airwallex are not licensed as banks or electronic payment institutions under Taiwans Financial Supervisory Commission legal framework; they cannot hold statutory corporate deposits, receive capital injection, perform foreign-exchange settlement or issue tax-recognised trade receipts onshore. They may only act as ancillary software/technical introducers to local licensed banks, and they are not a permissible substitute for a designated foreign-exchange bank for WFOE treasury obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors or the authorised local manager must appear physically at a designated bank branch with corporate chop, board resolution, original company registration certificate, unified business identification number, and proof of the approved foreign-investment permit. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for WFOE operating or escrow accounts; the banks AML/KYC compliance committee will normally require a face-to-face interview plus an on-site or video-recorded business substance review before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial-ownership chain passing through mainland China and Hong Kong with nominee shareholders and opaque tiering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Direct WFOE parent-structuring diagram, audited group consolidated financial statements, UBO declaration identifying all natural persons owning 25% or more, current share registry with individual shareholder identities, certified English translations of Chinese business licences and registration certificates, source-of-funds documentation for each historical share subscription, and signed bank references from the ultimate parents licensed bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-Delivery e-commerce model using logistics agents to collect cash, producing fragmented local-currency deposits and possible mingling of third-party collections
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed logistics cash-collection agency agreement, e-commerce platform order-level daily COD reconciliation reports, cash storage and branch deposit slips, internal cash-handling standard operating procedures, logistics delivery confirmation records, and a CPA-initiated revenue-recognition audit confirming no unrelated third-party funds pass through the WFOEs bank accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border remittances routed through third-party payment aggregators or foreign logistics firms with trade descriptions inconsistent with ISIC 4791 mail-order retail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial invoices describing the exact retail merchandise, packing lists, air waybill or bill-of-lading copies, final-mile delivery confirmation, customs export/import declarations, marketplace seller records, and SWIFT MT103 copies with consistent foreign-exchange purpose codes in field 70 matching the underlying online orders and logistics settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection arriving after incorporation in multiple tranches from various group accounts or without a matching Investment Commission permit and central-bank FX settlement declaration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved Investment Commission foreign-investor permit, copy of the approved remittance warrant, SWIFT MT103 messages showing the exact named remitter and legal beneficiary WFOE name, inward remittance credit advices, central-bank foreign-exchange transaction settlement report issued by the local designated bank, and a Taiwan CPA capital verification report signed within the statutory period confirming full subscription receipt.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT103 STP from the directly permitted foreign investor to the WFOEs NT-dollar or foreign-currency escrow account at a designated Bank of Taiwan branch. The payment must reference the central-bank foreign-exchange direct-investment purpose code for equity capital, and the remitter name must exactly match the foreign-investor permit holder. Immediately after receipt, the designated bank must be instructed to book the foreign-exchange transaction report and convert or retain the funds according to the investment permit. A Taiwan CPA must then issue the statutory capital verification report, typically within one month of remittance, and the original inward remittance advice, capital verification report and Investment Commission approval must be retained for tax filing, bank annual review and future dividend repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements from the WFOE operational account should use SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and logistics fee settlements under correct current-account purpose codes. Commercial letters of credit may be issued through Bank of Taiwan or Mega International Commercial Bank via SWIFT MT700 for bulk procurement or high-value inventory purchases, providing documentary protection and reconciled shipping documents. Documentary collections are acceptable for open-account or documents-against-payment trade where the counterparty and transport corridor are stable; for cash-on-delivery logistics disbursements, domestic NT-dollar payments should be made through local clearing rails, supplemented by SWIFT MT103 for offshore logistics and platform partners, with every payment backed by commercial invoices, order-level reconciliation, delivery proof and applicable tax invoices.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable New Taiwan dollar outright forward contracts with licensed designated foreign-exchange banks, supported by verified trade receivables, purchase orders and projected inventory flows and subject to central-bank reporting limits.

Cross-currency swaps with the same licensed onshore banks solely for documented trade financing, import/export working capital or approved direct-investment balance-sheet hedging, with no speculative leverage and with full underlying exposure evidence filed with the central bank.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards for non-NTD crosses only, entered into by the WFOE or its parent treasury through a licensed offshore counterparty as economic hedging of committed trade cash flows, without delivery of NTD at maturity and with independent confirmation that the hedge amount never exceeds the documented underlying exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership and Shareholding Variance Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 1 to March 31 each year for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Summary penalty of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000 per offense (approximately USD 320 to USD 1,600); if the company fails to rectify after a formal notice, the competent authority may order dissolution or initiate administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Regional National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 to May 31 of the year following the taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid tax bears an overdue charge at the annual postal savings interest rate plus a late surcharge assessment of up to 10% of the deficiency; failure to file even after a statutory notice can trigger an additional 20% surcharge and enforced collection, ultimately leading to an administrative order suspending business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Installment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Regional National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: September 1 to September 30 during the current taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the provisional installment is not filed, the company receives a two-week notice; continued failure imposes a penalty of NT$1,500 (approximately USD 50) per each failure and the entire assessed tax becomes immediately due, with possible seizure of assets or cancellation of the taxpayer's business registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 20 of the Taiwan Company Act and the Guidelines for Certified Public Accountant Audits of Company Financial Statements, a company must commission an independent certified audit when (1) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 950,000); or (2) annual operating revenue exceeds NT$100,000,000 (approximately USD 3,200,000); or (3) the company is a listed, public, or special-industry enterprise (banking, insurance, securities, etc.). Additionally, any WFOE engaged in cross-border e-commerce with cash-on-delivery collections that maintains foreign-exchange remittance flows above NTD thresholds set by the Central Bank of China (Taiwan) may be required to provide an audited statement to the regulatory authority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies apply IFRS exactly as published by the IASB. Non-public companies, including the target entity, apply the Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standard (a local GAAP equivalent to IFRS-for-SMEs) supplemented by the Regulations on Profit-Seeking Enterprise Taxation for all tax-return reconciliations; all statutory books are maintained in New Taiwan Dollars, books and records in Chinese or English are accepted by the authorities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each calendar year the company must file its annual beneficial ownership confirmation with the Department of Commerce between March 1 and March 31. The report must identify any natural person who directly or indirectly owns more than 25% of the company's shares or control, and must disclose any share transfers within the preceding year. For any ordinary share transfer or change in beneficial ownership occurring during the year, the company must update the statutory register and file the change with the Department of Commerce within 15 calendar days of the triggering event. Non-compliance is subject to fines imposed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and continuous violation may prevent the company from performing customs clearance or FX remittance under the target payment rails.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 900 per year for a commercial registered office/agent in Taiwan, plus USD 150 - USD 450 for licensed corporate secretarial handling of the annual filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 8,000 per year for a certified audit of a cross-border e-commerce mail-order operation transacting cash-on-delivery settlements

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan offers a 12% preferential rate on undistributed earnings retained beyond statutory limits; qualified R&D expenditures may enjoy a 15% tax credit (limited to 30% of the tax payable); approved emerging-market export services may apply for a 5-year tax holiday in free-trade-zone enterprises; no patent box regime currently exists; small and medium enterprises (SMEs) can benefit from a reduced rate of 20% on the first NT$200,000 and 20% on the excess.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form No. 111, business tax return via the Ministry of Finance electronic filing system 'Tax Internet Filing System' / eTax Portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., by May 31 for a calendar-year taxpayer); an extension of up to one additional month may be granted upon application for approved accountants.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide gross receipts from mail-order retail, including cash-on-delivery sales, minus sales returns and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Taiwan-sourced revenue; income derived from cross-border e-commerce serving Taiwan customers must be included. For a WFOE resident in Taiwan, worldwide income is taxable, but foreign-source income may be exempt if the 50% business-activity threshold is not met; exclude non-Taiwan-sourced COD sales if no PE in Taiwan and substantiated by title-transfer evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to merchandise sold, including logistics, inbound freight, packing, and cash-on-delivery collection fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate intercompany purchase costs from the Chinese parent or affiliate according to the arm's length principle; ensure transfer pricing adjustments are reflected in Box 2 if a TNMM or CUP test requires a year-end adjustment; retain customs declarations and logistic statements.

If gross margin deviates materially from comparable Taiwanese e-commerce companies, prepare a benchmarking study to substantiate the arm's length result; flag any abnormal margin erosion due to cross-border related-party transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General and administrative, selling, and operating expenses (e.g., warehouse rental, logistics, marketing, payment processing, and management fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow any expenses not properly substantiated or not incurred for the Taiwanese business; management fees paid to the China parent must satisfy the 'benefit test' and arm's length calculation; charge-backs for shared services must be supported by an intercompany agreement and cost allocation methodology.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains/losses, dividends received, and other non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from a PRC subsidiary are exempt if the equity participation ratio is 10% or more and the seller holds the shares for at least 12 months; mark-to-market FX gains on CNY/TWD balances must be recognized; any deemed interest on thin-capitalization loans from the China parent must be adjusted if the debt-to-equity ratio exceeds 3:1 (non-financial business).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after statutory reconciliation between book accounting and tax law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back disallowed expenses; subtract exempt income; verify that the 'Imputed Profit on Intra-Group Services' is not artificially inflated; for a WFOE with the China market route, ensure that all revenue from Taiwan operations is booked, and that no profit is shifted through offshore shell entities lacking economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The amount of prior-year losses legally deductible in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses from the previous 10 years may be carried forward; the 'same business and same tax jurisdiction' rule applies; any loss arising from a related-party transaction that fails the arm's length test will be disallowed.
This is the base for the 20% headline rate. If Box 8 is less than the statutory minimum threshold, consider the alternative minimum tax ('AMT') on book income if applicable.
No territorial apportionment; Taiwan taxes worldwide income of a resident WFOE. Ensure no double-tax relief is claimed without valid foreign tax credit certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, investment tax credits (R&D), and quarterly prepayments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits (FTC) are limited to the Taiwan tax on the same foreign-source income; for COD merchant collections routed through Airwallex or third-party payment processors, confirm the withholding tax credit eligibility in the payment-rail jurisdiction; treaty relief cannot be claimed at the corporate return level for outbound dividends, but for inbound interest/royalty paid to Taiwan, use the credit mechanism if a DTA applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 9 minus Box 10, rounded to the nearest NT dollar.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If payment is not made by May 31, a late payment surcharge of 1% every two days up to 15% of the un-paid tax applies; criminal evasion is triggered if intentional understatement exceeds the statutory threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without extension: a 3% surcharge on the unpaid tax per two days, up to 9%, plus a late interest rate (postal savings rate) from the original deadline; understatement of taxable income of more than NT$100,000 or 10% triggers a two-tier penalty: 0.5 times the understated tax for voluntary disclosure, 1 time if discovered by the tax authority, and up to 2.5 times for intentional fraud; criminal liability for tax evasion: imprisonment for up to 5 years and/or a fine of up to NT$6,000,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed to a non-resident shareholder (including a Chinese parent company); under the 2024 amendment, the rate remains 21% (plus a possible additional retained-earnings surtax of 5% on undistributed earnings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Claiming DTA relief for dividends paid to a Taiwanese shareholder from China would use the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation (not yet in force as of the knowledge cutoff); therefore, no reduced WHT is available. For any future entering into force, the protocol is: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Taiwan tax authority; (2) complete the applicable Certificate of Residence form; (3) submit a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient is the actual owner and does not pass through a conduit entity; (4) provide a certificate of the shareholder's paid-in capital and dividend income details; (5) file the treaty relief application with the Taiwan withholding agent before the payment date; if all conditions are met, the WHT rate may be reduced from 21% to 10% (dividend participation threshold of at least 25% for 12 months), but given the current non-force of the cross-strait agreement, no treaty relief is currently possible.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-resident corporate lenders: statutory WHT 20% (or 15% if the recipient is a Taiwanese branch with a banking license); royalties paid to a non-resident for intellectual property: statutory WHT 20%; if a relevant tax treaty with the recipient's jurisdiction applies, interest may be reduced to 0-10%, royalties to 0-10% (e.g., US-Taiwan has no treaty; Taiwan’s DTA network covers limited countries; China-Taiwan treaty is not yet operational). For payments to the Chinese parent, the 20% WHT on royalties and interest applies unless a special cross-strait arrangement is in effect.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File must be prepared if the total intercompany related-party transactions exceed NT$50 million (for purchases) or NT$20 million (for sales), or if the entity engages in controlled transactions with a related party located in a low-tax jurisdiction, or if intangible-related transactions exceed NT$20 million; a Master File is required if total consolidated group revenue exceeds NT$30 billion and the group has cross-border transactions; the Annual Transfer Pricing Report (Form 105) must be filed with the tax return.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) are not directly enacted in Taiwan, but the 'substance over form' doctrine applies under Article 12-1 of the Tax Collection Act (anti-avoidance principle). The tax authority may re-characterize a transaction if the arrangement lacks 'reasonable commercial purpose' or 'economic substance' (e.g., a Hong Kong intermediary without employees, assets, or operational risks used solely to re-invoice COD sales). Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) concept is applied through the permanent establishment threshold and the essential business-function analysis: to qualify for treaty benefits or to avoid a Taiwanese business income tax, the WFOE must prove that its sales activities, customer support, payment processing, and risk-bearing are performed in Taiwan; otherwise, profits are deemed attributable to a Taiwanese PE and fully taxable. Foreign companies with no Taiwanese PE are not subject to Taiwan corporate income tax, but if the entity is a Taiwan-resident WFOE, it is taxed on worldwide income regardless of economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsifying cash-on-delivery revenue records by underreporting sales receipts from COD logistics partners, or using offshore payment processors to divert Taiwan-source income without reconciliation to local logistic remittance reports, causing understated taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 110 of the Tax Collection Act: penalty equal to 0.5 times the underpaid tax if voluntary, 1 time if ordinary negligence, and 2.5 times if intentional; in addition, interest is assessed at the postal postal deposit rate for late payment; criminal evasion under Article 109 of the Business Tax Act for fraudulent VAT filings; for income tax, Article 41 of the Income Tax Act: a prison term of up to 5 years and/or fines up to NT$6,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns or direct the creation of false invoices are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; the tax authority may apply for provisional seizure of personal assets, prohibition on transfers, and exit bans (blacklisting) under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act for unpaid taxes exceeding NT$1,000,000; criminal conviction may carry imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years, and a director may lose the right to serve as a director of any Taiwanese company for a period of up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham Interposition and Transfer Pricing Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing COD sales through a related Hong Kong or BVI company that lacks real employees, premises, and operational risks, solely to shift profits away from Taiwan, or setting transfer prices for intercompany logistics and platform fees that do not meet OECD arm's length standards without preparing a Local File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 12-1 of the Tax Collection Act empowers the tax authority to re-characterize the transaction, disallow the deductions, and assess tax with an additional penalty of up to 1.5 times the basic tax due; the Transfer Pricing Assessment Rules (2019 amendment) impose documentation penalties of NT$30,000 to NT$300,000 for failure to provide, and additional adjustments under Article 114-1 of the Income Tax Act; criminal liability for document forgery if false agreements are created.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be required to personally refund the re-characterized profits if the company becomes insolvent; a travel ban is automatically triggered under Article 33 of the Tax Collection Act for directors of companies with tax arrears above NT$10,000,000; the director’s personal assets are reachable if the court pierces the corporate veil due to commingling of funds, and imprisonment of up to 7 years can be imposed under Article 342 of the Criminal Code for breach of trust by acting against the company’s interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the cash-on-delivery logistics remittance channel without documented customer identity verification, failing to integrate with the AML system in the jurisdiction of the target market, or receiving COD cash proceeds in an emerging-market country through local logistics partners and then transferring the funds through Airwallex or other intermediaries without proper AML declarations (structuring transactions below the reporting threshold to evade anti-money laundering scrutiny).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act: administrative fines of NT$1,000,000 to NT$10,000,000 for failing to conduct Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and record-keeping; criminal penalties for money laundering: incarceration of up to 7 years and fines up to NT$50,000,000 if the proceeds originate from a predicate offense; if the emerging-market jurisdiction imposes its own AML fines, the WFOE may face parallel liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Money Laundering Control Act, directors who intentionally ignore suspicious transaction reports may be sentenced to 7 years’ imprisonment; the company's authorization to operate may be revoked; directors' personal bank accounts may be frozen and travel bans (blacklisting) applied by the Financial Supervisory Commission; if the corporate veil is pierced on the grounds of 'nominal management' or 'abusive veil', the director is personally liable for civil restitution of the laundered amount and criminal fines.
